subject: Stated minimum true-up, exit waterfall, and credit tapering - order form redline
messages:
From: Daniel Park <dpark@nimbushealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Ana Mendez <amendez@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2025-06-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify stated minimum true-up waterfall + exit credits on order form

Irene —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement ran the draft order form past our finance/legal teams and we have two areas that need clearer language before we can move to signature:

1) Stated minimum / true-up waterfall: we need a clear definition of how the stated minimum applies across partial quarters and during ramp periods. The current Exhibit B references quarterly true-up but is silent on proration and sequencing when usage spikes within the quarter. Can Redwood confirm whether the true-up applies pro rata to the partial quarter or to the full quarter in which usage occurred?

2) Exit waterfall / clawback: we accept a short ramp clawback but need a predictable tapering schedule if Nimbus reduces committed usage during the first 12 months. The redline we received earlier had a flat 12-month clawback — procurement is asking for a staged taper (e.g., 80% in Q1, 60% in Q2, 40% in Q3, 0% thereafter). They also want an absolute cap on clawback dollars tied to three months' average spend.

3) Credits and migration carve-out: if Nimbus migrates workloads to another region or vendor for regulatory reasons, we want a migration credit so short-term disruption doesn't trigger full clawback.

Can someone on your side propose explicit language for these items we can send to our counsel? Ideally we’d like a short redline and a one-page summary of the economic effect so we can run it through our CFO.

Thanks,
Daniel
Procurement Manager
Nimbus Health

[Attachment: procurement_redline_notes.txt (summary of asks)]

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <dpark@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-20T13:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify stated minimum true-up waterfall + exit credits on order form

Daniel —

Appreciate the clear list. We pulled legal and finance into thread to get you a concise proposal. High-level responses below and we’ve attached a redline (Exhibit B) and a one-page economic matrix.

- True-up proration: Redwood proposes pro rata true-ups for partial quarters during ramp. We will add explicit language: "True-ups will be calculated pro rata for any partial billing period during the initial 6-month ramp window; thereafter true-ups are applied on a full-quarter basis."

- Exit/clawback taper: We can accept a staged tapering schedule but suggest limiting the maximum clawback to 75% of the remaining stated minimum to balance our capacity reservation. Proposed schedule: Q1 75%, Q2 50%, Q3 25%, Q4+ 0%. This preserves runway while giving Nimbus predictable diminishing liability. We also propose an absolute cap equal to three months' average billed spend as measured over the trailing 3 months prior to termination.

- Migration credit: We can include a migration carve-out if the disruption is driven by documented regulatory constraints or force majeure-like controls (e.g., mandatory data residency change requiring vendor switch). Proposed: 60-day migration credit on a pro rata basis, not exceeding two months' committed fees.

Next steps: 
- Attached redline: "Redwood_Orderform_ExhibitB_pricing_v3_redline.docx" with tracked edits.
- Short economic matrix: "TrueUp-Waterfall-Proposal.pdf" showing sample scenarios and dollar impact.

If this tradeoff is workable, legal (Karthik) will follow with final contract language. If not, we can schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through details.

Best,
Irene
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

[Attachment: Redwood_Orderform_ExhibitB_pricing_v3_redline.docx]

From: Daniel Park <dpark@nimbushealth.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Ana Mendez <amendez@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2025-06-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify stated minimum true-up waterfall + exit credits on order form

Irene —

Thanks — the proposed direction is helpful. A couple quick responses after running the numbers with our CFO:

- Q1/Q2 taper vs your proposed Q1/Q2 numbers: CFO prefers steeper front-loading for us (80% then 60%) but would accept your 75%/50% if the absolute cap on clawback dollars is set to two months' average spend instead of three. That reduces potential high-dollar downside for Nimbus.

- Migration carve-out: procurement is fine with the 60-day pro rata credit provided Redwood also agrees to reasonable documentation (regulatory notice + 30-day remediation window).

- Proration window: can we narrow the pro rata ramp window to 3 months instead of 6? Our usage ramps fast and CFO argues the 6-month window overstates commitment.

If Redwood agrees to: (a) 75%/50%/25% taper, (b) cap clawback at two months' average billed spend, and (c) 3-month pro rata ramp window, Nimbus will sign the redline and send to counsel.

If you prefer a call, Marissa — can you take 15 minutes to align?

-Daniel

Daniel / team —

I reviewed the attached redline and the economic matrix. Quick legal points and the exact proposed contract language we intend to add (summary below). We tried to balance Nimbus's requests and Redwood's need to manage reserved capacity exposure.

1) Proration (ramp window) — final proposal: 3-month pro rata ramp window. Addition to Exhibit B: "For the initial three (3) calendar months following the Effective Date (the \"Ramp Period\"), stated minimums will be pro rated for any partial billing period. Thereafter, true-ups will be applied on a full-quarter basis."

2) Tapered clawback schedule & cap — final proposal: 75% (Q1), 50% (Q2), 25% (Q3), 0% thereafter; AND a cap equal to two (2) months' average billed spend (measured over the trailing three months prior to termination). Contract language to be inserted in Section 4.2.

3) Migration carve-out — accepted with documentation: regulatory notice + 30-day remediation; credit limited to a maximum of two (2) months' committed fees. Language to be added to force majeure / early termination carve-outs.

4) Implementation detail: we will include a worked example in Exhibit B (sample math for a 6-month ramp, sudden 40% drop in Q2, and how cap applies).

If Nimbus confirms acceptance of the three items above, we will send a clean redline and a short execution checklist for signatures. If there are remaining commercial asks (different cap, alternate taper) we can loop in Ben for finance-level concessions.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
